notes: A clean four-rung ladder. The line above bullet 1 ('You must zone after completing the previous Quest') is a precondition, not a rung, and the runtime cannot see zoning anyway. Every sub-bullet under 1 is a dialogue menu; the 'Total Loser' title branch is an outcome and the page itself says you can get the title later regardless, so it is not a step. Bullet 3's Cermet Door is a real targetable entity and resolves, which is why step 3 keeps a marker where a bare 'check the door' would not. The hazard sub-bullet under 3 is genuine and worth the note rather than a rung: killing too many monsters in Fei'Yin while carrying the new spell turns it into 'Shantotto's ex-spell' -- a DIFFERENT key item id -- so the evidence on step 2 will silently read false and the mark will fall back to Torino-Samarino, which is exactly where the page tells you to go. The single bullet under 'After the walkthrough: Notes' is about unlocking Shantotto's Trust and is not a step.

notes: Red Mage AF1. 'Repeatable: af' is the artifact-armour category leaking into the field and means false. The header spells the key 'Dav. Storage Key' and the walkthrough 'Davoi Storage Key'; both resolve to the same item, and the longer form is used. The Storage Hole is a real targetable entity and resolves, but it MOVES at the change of every game day among fifteen listed spots, so the step deliberately carries no grid -- one wrong grid would be worse than none. notes:
The Empyreal Arrow weapon-skill quest. Two judgement calls.

First, the key item. Bullet 2 grants both the key item the page calls 'Weapons Training Guide' and the item Bow of Trials. The game's key item 343 is 'weapon training guide', SINGULAR, so the wiki's spelling does not resolve and writing the game's spelling would be inventing a name the page never uses. The Bow of Trials is granted in the same breath, resolves, and is what the next step consumes, so it carries step 1's evidence and the guide is left out entirely. Nothing is lost: both arrive together.

Second, the latent. Bullet 2's sub-bullet is a bare 'Breaking the Latent' -- a transclusion the prepass could not expand (the page carries the transclusion flag), so the rendered text says nothing at all about how to break it. It is NOT given a rung of its own, because steps 1 and 3 are both Perih Vashai and wedging an unmarkable, unobservable rung between two steps on the same NPC is exactly the shape the pilot warned about: the mark would sit on nothing instead of pointing you back at her. It is step 2's note.

Bullet 1 is a precondition (you may not hold two Weapon Skill quests) and not a step. Bullet 4 is pure routing into Cape Teriggan and merges into the ??? it leads to. Bullet 6 is a fight AND a second examine of the same ???, so it splits. 'Archery skill 250+' has no slot and nothing observable, so it is flagged and gates nothing; the 'Level 71' beside it is the level gate, since the Level field itself is empty.

steps.note: bullet 1 is a precondition: quit any other Weapon Skill quest with its own giver first. She hands over the Bow of Trials and the key item the page spells 'Weapons Training Guide' -- see the quest note for why only the Bow is used as evidence.

notes:
The whole walkthrough is a wikitable, so there are no [n] numbers to cite. The seven '*' items inside it are numbered 1..7 in the order they appear and source_bullets refers to that numbering: 1 talk, 2 get the key, 3 find a chest, 4 open it, 5 return, 6 name the spot, 7 collect after midnight. Items 3 and 4 are one action -- you cannot 'locate' a chest as a separate rung the player can be past -- and 6 and 7 are the tail of item 5's conversation, so four steps come out of seven.

The chest's spawn points are given only as blue squares on two map images, which do not survive rendering, so step 3 carries the zone and no grid. That is the honest answer: a made-up grid would point players at one of several spots.

'Promathia Mission 4-3 flag' sits in Quest Reqs, not in a Previous field the page does not even have, and the page marks it unverified twice over -- it is recorded in prev so a human can see it, where an unresolvable title reads as 'unverifiable' rather than 'blocked'. Fame is 'o' with FLevel 'unknown/none': neither is one of the nine regions, so the gate is raw-only. The reward arriving 'after midnight (next game day)' is a cooldown, not a step.

notes:
Ranger AF1, and one of the better-behaved pages in this batch: nine bullets, seven steps, three evidence points across three zones. 'Repeatable: af' is the artifact-armour category and means false.

Bullets 2 and 4 are not steps: bullet 2 is Perih Vashai telling you where to go and bullet 4 is Perchond explaining what Semih Lafihna asked him, which is how you learn about the pond -- narration, folded into the steps they set up. Nobody named Semih Lafihna is ever interacted with; the quest's description says you hand her the earring but the walkthrough never does, and she is not recorded as a target anywhere because she is never there.

The drop is called 'Glittersand' in bullet 5 and 'Pinch of Glittersand' in bullet 6; they are the same item and the longer form is used. Alexius' line about needing a full moon is contradicted by the page's own sub-bullet, so the ??? step says so rather than carrying an unobservable moon gate.

notes:
The quest shuttles between two Ranpi-Monpis with the same name -- the past one in Windurst Waters (S) (E-9) and the present one in Windurst Waters -- and every step alternates between them, so the zone on each step is doing all the work of telling them apart. The page gives no grid for the present-day one, so that field stays null rather than borrowing (E-9) from the other era.

The 'After the walkthrough: Summary' section is not steps -- it just restates the four ingredients -- but it is where the fourth one is spelled 'Stick of Pepperoni', which is the form that resolves; the header's 'Pepperoni' is the same item.

The one real compromise is step 4. The page says to trade the four ingredients and 'wait one game day for the dish to be completed', then jumps straight to 'After receiving [KI] Ranpi-Monpi Specialty' without ever saying how it reaches you -- the only thing it says about speaking to him again in that window is that it is extra dialogue. So the Specialty is recorded as step 4's evidence rather than being given an invented 'talk to him again' rung. It arrives late by a game day, which nothing observable reports; the mark simply stays on the present-day Ranpi-Monpi until it does, which is where you want to be standing anyway. Quest demoted to medium for that gap. The three '(Optional) Speak to him again' sub-bullets are all extra dialogue and none is a step.

notes:
The Scholar level-75 limit break. There is nobody to talk to anywhere in this quest: it starts by ZONING into Xarcabard, the middle is a drop off orcs, and it ends in a battlefield. The header's giver, 'Prof. Schultz', is the battlefield's boss, not a standing entity -- so this is the Blade of Evil shape and step 1 is a deliberately unmarkable zone entry.

The header string is kept in start.npc anyway, exactly as Blade of Evil keeps Zeid. It is the only name the page offers, no step in this quest is markable, and a start that resolves to nothing at all would drop the quest from the index entirely and lose the ladder with it. A key that never matches a live entity in the field costs nothing; it simply never draws.

Bullet 3's door is named only as 'the door' -- no name, so no target, per the rule. Its zone is null, not Throne Room: Throne Room is a separate instanced zone that the door opens INTO, so recording it on the trade would place the step in a zone the player has not entered yet and cannot trade from. The page names no other zone there, and with no target to mark, null costs nothing. Step 4, the fight, is genuinely in the Throne Room. Bullet 4's sub-bullets are all tactics. The 'After the walkthrough: Notes' bullet says the quest is skippable if you already hold New Worlds Await, which is a fact about the level cap and not a step. The page calls the boss 'Schultz' in bullet 4 and 'Prof. Schultz' in the header; the fuller form is used for the mob. The orc names are pluralised in the page and recorded singular, which is how they are named in the field.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 4: you win at roughly 20% of Schultz's HP and the Grimoire never has to die, so its 'kill' role is the closest the schema has.

steps.note: zoning in fires the cutscene -- there is nobody to speak to. Survival Guide or Teleport-Vahzl both count. You must wait for the game day after Seeing Blood-red before it will trigger, which nothing observable reports.

the page calls it only 'the door' and names no zone but the Throne Room it opens onto, so there is no target to mark. The Throne Room is the instanced battlefield the door leads INTO; the cutscene and the trade both happen at the door, one zone short of it, in a zone the page never names -- so the zone is left null rather than recorded as the place you are not yet standing in. A cutscene fires at the door first, then the trade starts the fight. All buffs are stripped on entry and your subjob is disabled; Trusts need the Rhapsody in Umber key item.
Open fast both buff themselves if left alone and neither sleeps reliably. The Grimoire has far less HP and is worth killing first without Trusts; Valaineral tends to end it outright with Uriel Blade.

notes:
Samurai AF head. Eleven bullets, ten steps, and the ladder is genuinely long: four talks in four zones before anything observable happens at all.

The header writes the giver 'Jaucribaix / Gilgamesh' -- one Norg entity under two names, and the walkthrough only ever says Jaucribaix, so that is what every step targets. The header puts him at (L-8) and bullet 1 at (K-8); both are kept where each was written rather than reconciled.

Bullet 4's door is named only as 'the door on the lower level in Bastok Mines (J-6)', so it gets no target -- the grid and the note carry it instead. That is a real loss of a marker and it is flagged, but a made-up door name would resolve to nothing anyway. The closed-door caveat is the sort of thing that costs an hour, so it is in the note verbatim.

Bullets 9 and 10 are one action on one NPC -- he asks for the Gold Thread and you trade it -- and are merged; a separate 'talk' rung would be a ladder position on the same NPC in the same spot that no packet could ever distinguish. Bullet 11's 'zone out of Norg, then return' is a real precondition on the final talk and stays a note, since zoning is invisible to the addon. The sub-bullet about tossing the Banishing Charm afterwards is an outcome.
